_authoredBlocks: Everything prefixed `_` below is AUTHORED CONTENT, transcribed from docs/content-bible.md with a per-entry source. It lives here rather than in data/ because data/ is Lane A's and carries no art copy; it is the art lane's transcription of the bible, subject to G2 exactly as data/ is.
_seedRule: seed = pin ?? hashSeed(version, id) using core/rng.ts's FNV-1a (§8.1's own hash — no second generator, G11). A row's seed is therefore a pure function of its id and its version, which is what makes G5 mechanical: regenerating an asset re-derives the SAME seed, and the only way to get a different one is to bump `version`, which is the manifest-entry versioning §8.4 licenses. `recordedSeed` freezes the seed actually used the first time a row produced a file; the runner refuses to submit a different seed for that row unless the version moved (SeedReuseError).

_deviations.finding: 154 battle sprites is arithmetically impossible against the shipped roster. data/species.json holds 27 lines of which 3 are Ancients; 24 aging lines × 3 age forms + 3 Ancients × 1 form = 75 forms × front/back = 150.
_deviations.action: The manifest derives 150 creature-battle rows from data/species.json. This is DEVIATIONS.md D2, already logged by Lane A; recorded here because §9.7's number is the one an art reviewer counts against.

_deviations.finding: rembg is a Python/ONNX salient-object segmenter; it is not installed, it is not deterministic across versions, and it is not idempotent — a second pass re-mattes an already-matted sprite.
_deviations.action: Background removal is a border flood fill against the flat generated background key. Every prompt ends in `plain white background` (the §9.2 skeleton, verbatim), so the background is a known flat key, not an unknown photograph. The fill is exact, deterministic and idempotent, which is what §9.3's own 'every step idempotent' clause requires and what §10.4's idempotency test measures. If a class ever generates on a non-flat background, that class needs a real matte and this note is where to start.

_deviations.finding: §9.3's chain starts at 'nearest-neighbour downscale to target'. The raw outputs are 1024² frames containing a subject that occupies a fraction of the canvas; downscaling that to 96² yields a creature ~20px tall floating in white.
_deviations.action: A trim-to-content step runs BEFORE step 1 for the sprite classes (declared per class as `postprocess.trim`), and the downscale then fits the trimmed subject into the target frame preserving aspect. §9.3's three named steps keep their order and their semantics; this is an addition, not a reordering. Maps and painted dex do not trim.

_deviations.finding: Two post-process target sizes named in §9.3 — battle 96² and mini 32² — have no home in data/balance.json, unlike the overworld character size (balance.map.playerSpriteW/H), the map size (balance.map.mapNativePx) and the prop scale (balance.map.propInteractionRadiusDefault).
_deviations.action: They ship as `targetW`/`targetH` on the class specs in this file, which is the art lane's data file. tests/unit/manifest.test.ts binds every class target that DOES have a balance source to that source, so the three sizes that are shared with the game can never drift; the two that are art-only are reviewable in one place. Raised for Lane A: `balance.map.battleSpritePx` and `balance.map.miniSpritePx` would close it.

_deviations.finding: L6 says the string `green shirt, ranger cap with star badge, leather satchel, walking boots` appears VERBATIM in every player prompt. The prompt that actually produced the gate-B0-approved sprite does not contain it verbatim — it elaborates: `a green shirt, brown shorts, a peaked green ranger cap with a small yellow star badge, a leather satchel on a shoulder strap, and brown walking boots`.
_deviations.action: The approved prompt wins, and this is why: §8.4 and G5 make an approved asset's prompt+seed its identity, and the approved sprite is the one Hank signed off at a SUPERVISED gate. Substituting the L6 string would generate a different character while claiming to be a regeneration — the exact failure G5 exists to prevent. Every L6 ELEMENT is present (green shirt · ranger cap · star badge · leather satchel · walking boots) and the cape ban is enforced on the negative side (B-D7), so L6's intent holds; only its 'verbatim' clause does not. `_player.l6Verbatim` keeps the spec string on the record, and tests/unit/manifest.test.ts asserts the elements plus byte-equality with manifest-b0.json's approved row.
